newsitem.title: KENYA: Power monopoly boosts Nairobi bourse index.
newsitem.headline: Power monopoly boosts Nairobi bourse index.

text.p: A 60,000-share deal on the special one-hour hold board for power monopoly Kenya Power & Lighting Co at 171 from 165 boosted the Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) 20-share index on Monday, floor dealers said.

They said the index went up 27.30 points to stand at 3261.05. Turnover was posted at 22.304 million shillings traded on 359,105 shares from 10.640 million shillings traded on 370,385 shares on Friday.
Brokers said there was competitive bidding for the power share driven by rumours of an intended bonus issue at around the same time as company results, expected before March.
"The company is going through a restructuring programme and since it does not have money, it might choose to issue bonus shares to raise funds," one broker said.
Last Tuesday, the power firm's capitalisation stood at 2.461 billion shillings. The price has been upward bound boosted heavily by foreign demand. It began the year at 141.
Another broker said a scarcity of shares and persistent belief that at the current price the shares were undervalued had helped push Kenya Power & Lighting Co higher.
Across the board, prices in key shares improved marginally.
There has been speculation about anticipated end-year results which has resulted in heavy buying in the market, especially for the financials.
"Funds are also shifting to the stock exchange from the primary market because many investors expect treasury bill rates to keep dropping," one broker said.
Financials traded heavily, with Barclays Bank closing at 110 from 106 while Standard Chartered Bank gained 3.0 to close at 53.50.
Kenya Airways edged to 9.70 from 9.50 while Uchumi Supermarket traded at 55 unchanged.
In the agriculturals, Rea Vipingo closed at 10.75 from 10.50.
